clue.text: Just a moment, back in half a second

definitions.text: Just a moment, back in half a second

parts.words: Just a moment, back in half a second
parts.note: someone stepping out promises to return almost at once, in the instant it takes a camera bulb to go off

explanation.surface: Someone stepping away asks for a moment and promises to be right back.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an instant, as in the phrase promising return in no time at all.

clue.text: No paying guest has this room above water

parts.note: something with no paying is free of charge
a lodger has board, meals provided at the house

explanation.surface: A lodger who pays nothing gets a room with a sea view.
explanation.walkthrough: A non-paying guest gets FREE BOARD; whole, it is the nautical term for the height of deck above the waterline.
explanation.definitionFit: On a vessel this term names the height of hull standing clear of the waterline, the margin of dry room above the sea.

clue.text: A chap embracing one violently

indicators.note: the chap is said to embrace or hug the next piece, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a chap is a man
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man hugs somebody with excessive force.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning with full force or vehemently.

clue.text: Gentleman John in Nova Scotia

definitions.meaning: John ..., Gentleman is a Victorian novel by Dinah Craik, whose hero is John ...
the capital city of the Canadian province of Nova Scotia

explanation.surface: A gentleman called John lives in eastern Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the title hero of Craik's novel and the provincial capital share this surname, also a Yorkshire town.

clue.text: Military position moved into a tent

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier's stance is shifted inside a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing upright, heels together, is the drill stance soldiers call by this name.

clue.text: In France, have you a note that's sharp?

parts.note: French for 'have you?' is as-tu
te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A French speaker asks whether you have a keen note.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd or quick-witted, a synonym for mentally keen.

clue.text: Nine of them will appear as three-quarters

definitions.text: Nine of them will appear as three-quarters

parts.words: Nine of them will appear as three-quarters
parts.note: a fraction puzzle: nine parts of a whole cut into twelve equal slices make the same as 3/4

explanation.surface: Some unnamed set of nine pieces adds up to three quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine parts in twelve equal three in four, so these fractional slices fit the arithmetic.

clue.text: Somewhat cloudy, this hypo thesis?

definitions.meaning: hazy or misty, like a nebula
the theory that the solar system condensed from a gas cloud is known by this adjective plus hypothesis, split here as 'hypo thesis'

explanation.surface: A rather cloudy idea is offered as a hypothesis.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to nebulae, hence misty, and names Laplace's theory of planetary origin.

clue.text: To be exasperating, I wore mink in the restaurant

parts.note: someone dressed in mink is in fur
taken as written
what one does in a restaurant: ate

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to wearing mink while dining out, which annoyed people.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the order IN FUR, I, ATE: 'in fur I ate' says I wore mink and dined in the restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: To madden or enrage someone is to exasperate them.

clue.text: Vote against holding race; get smart

indicators.note: the vote holds the race within it, surrounding it

parts.note: a vote against is a nay
TT, the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Opposing a vote while a race is on is a smart move.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and stylishly dressed, as in a dapper suit.

clue.text: Eastern girl's dress ornament

parts.note: Paulette is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An oriental young woman owns a decoration for her clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder piece on a uniform, a decorative trimming on military dress.

clue.text: Suit; about a month it takes to make

indicators.note: about signals turning the month's abbreviation round

parts.note: Feb is short for February
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tailor says a suit takes about a month to make.
explanation.definitionFit: To be appropriate or proper for, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Reading-based immunity

parts.note: in old English law a literate offender could escape secular trial by reading a Bible verse, so literacy bought legal protection

explanation.surface: A protection from harm is granted on the basis of reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Medieval courts handed clerics to church courts; proof of being a cleric became the ability to read Psalm 51, the 'neck verse'.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical privilege exempting the literate, at first priests, from the death penalty of lay courts.

clue.text: Extension of a letter, say

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is spoken aloud

parts.note: an X, an example of a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone describes an extension added to a letter, such as a postscript.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'an X' gives the word for a building add-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing or outbuilding added to a main building.

clue.text: Telling no one, Jack hurried up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the whole run of pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
a jack is a sailor, a tar
hurried means ran

explanation.surface: A sailor raced off without telling anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NO I TAR RAN as a whole into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating a story or account, the act of narrating.

clue.text: Want a label in the Strand

indicators.note: the label is put in the strand, within its letters

parts.note: a strand is a beach or shore
a label is a tag

explanation.surface: Someone wants a name badge in London's Strand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a London street, but here it is the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Want here means a lack or scarcity of something.

clue.text: Rebuit ten times, a cafe

indicators.note: a misprint of 'rebuilt': the words are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A café has been rebuilt ten times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebuit' (printed so, for 'rebuilt') rearranges TEN TIMES A.
explanation.definitionFit: A small French bar or bistro serving drinks and simple food.

clue.text: It holds the blade of a by no means striking poet

parts.note: a scab is a worker who refuses to strike
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: The blade belongs to a poet who would never join a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' suggests impressive, but means joining a strike: a strikebreaker is a SCAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath for a sword or dagger.

clue.text: Articles from abroad, caught in it, abandoned

parts.note: der is German for the and el is Spanish for the, both foreign definite articles

indicators.note: caught goes inside the word it

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Foreign goods caught in a trap were left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserted and left to decay, like a ship or building given up by its owner.

clue.text: Inspection of river rising in Cornish resort

indicators.note: the river is placed in the resort

parts.note: Looe is a seaside town in Cornwall

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising reads the river from bottom to top

parts.note: the Esk is a river in England and Scotland

explanation.surface: Inspectors examine a river that rises in a Cornish seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ESK into KSE, which goes inside LOOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal for a quick look or survey.

clue.text: Missing sailors — ten adrift

parts.note: ABs are able seamen

indicators.note: adrift means out of position, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Ten sailors are absent, their boat drifting.
explanation.definitionFit: Not present, a synonym for away.

clue.text: Doctor in eastern island about to be a sword-bearer

indicators.note: the doctor goes in the island

parts.note: Bali is an Indonesian island
c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A doctor on an Eastern island is about to carry a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt worn over the shoulder to carry a sword.

clue.text: Lethargy ruined Proust

indicators.note: ruined means the name's letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: The French novelist is ruined by lethargy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dazed, torpid state of near unconsciousness.

clue.text: Flora, a leading light

definitions.meaning: a plant of the lily family with star-shaped white flowers
the star that guided the Magi to Christ's birthplace

explanation.surface: A woman called Flora is a prominent figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the white-flowered plant and the guiding star of the Nativity bear this name.

clue.text: One in bed's getting up, indifferent to pain

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up reads the letters from bottom to top
in places the numeral for one inside the beds, so the beds surround it

parts.note: a cot is a bed
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone in bed gets up, unbothered by pain.
explanation.walkthrough: I inside COTS gives CIOTS; 'getting up' turns it over.
explanation.definitionFit: Enduring hardship without complaint, as the Greek philosophers taught.

clue.text: It's difficult with nothing held in stock

indicators.note: nothing is held in the word for difficult

parts.note: difficult means hard
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: It is hard to manage with nothing held in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden store or cache of goods.

clue.text: Skipper does from half of it

definitions.text: Skipper does from half of it

parts.words: Skipper does from half of it
parts.note: a skipper, someone who skips parts of a text, leaves out half of it

explanation.surface: A captain does something from half of an unnamed thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipper' looks like a ship's captain, but is one who skips pages.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave out or skip parts of something, which is what a skimming reader does.

clue.text: Relate to a forward in physical distress

indicators.note: forward goes in the physical distress

parts.note: pain is physical distress
forward means pert, cheeky

explanation.surface: Someone empathises with a football forward who is hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' suggests a footballer, but means cheeky: PERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong or pertain to something, a formal verb.

clue.text: One who strives to steer a boat

parts.note: to con a ship is to steer it
a tender is a small boat serving a ship

explanation.surface: Someone works hard to pilot a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor or rival who fights for victory.

clue.text: Young trainee acted badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are poorly arranged and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A young recruit gave a poor performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A student at a military or police academy.
